mainTopic: Who may eat a בכור בעל מום, and how much holiness blemished קדשים keep
overview: This amud discusses who may eat a בכור that has a blemish (בכור בעל מום) and how such an animal must be treated. בית הלל use a קל וחומר from a טמא כהן to prove that a זר may eat it, and they defend it by saying we compare only eating, not service. רבי עקיבא goes further and allows even a גוי, learning from 'כצבי וכאיל'. The other תנא needs every mention of 'צבי ואיל' for other lessons. Next, a ברייתא brings a מחלוקת about feeding a blemished בכור to נדות. בית שמאי forbid it, and they allow only טומאה from outside the body, using a proof from קרבן פסח. בית הלל permit it, because the פסוק says plain 'טמא'. Finally, a ברייתא forbids skinning a בכור or פסולי המוקדשין from the feet. רב חסדא says the בכור clause follows בית שמאי and the פסולי המוקדשין clause follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, because a בכור's holiness from birth may be uniquely strong.

steps.title: בית הלל limit the earlier source to an unblemished בכור
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל reply that the source limiting the בכור to כהנים only speaks about a תם. For a בעל מום, the פסוק says 'the impure and the pure may eat it alike.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל would answer: That only applies to an unblemished firstborn. But about a blemished firstborn it is written: 'The impure and the pure may eat it alike.'
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל answer the source that was used against them. They say it only talks about a perfect בכור, not one with a blemish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier source said the בכור belongs to the כהן. בית הלל agree, but only for a תם, which is brought on the מזבח. A בעל מום has its own פסוק, which treats it more like regular meat that the טמא and the טהור eat together.

keyTerms.meaning: This applies only to (the case just mentioned)
An unblemished animal, fit for the מזבח
An animal with a blemish, not fit for the מזבח
The ritually impure and the ritually pure

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel [would respond]:
This statement applies only to an unblemished [firstborn],
phrases.notes: "This statement" points back to the source that was used earlier to say the בכור is only for כהנים.

phrases.english: but about a blemished one it is written:
"The impure and the pure may eat it alike."

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית הִלֵּל: הָנֵי מִילֵּי תָּם, אֲבָל בַּעַל מוּם כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the proof of בית שמאי from the previous part of the sugya.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to a narrower case (תם only)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The source giving the בכור to כהנים seems to cover every בכור, even one with a blemish.
steps.terutzMaskana: That source covers only a תם. A בעל מום falls under a different פסוק that allows wider eating.

steps.title: בית הלל's קל וחומר from an impure כהן to a non-כהן
steps.stepSummary: If a טמא כהן, who cannot eat קדשים קלים, may eat a בכור בעל מום, then surely a זר, who may eat קדשים קלים, may eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If an impure כהן, who may not eat offerings of lesser holiness, may still eat a blemished firstborn, then a non-כהן, who may eat offerings of lesser holiness, should surely be allowed to eat a blemished firstborn.
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל build a קל וחומר to prove that a זר may eat a בכור בעל מום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק already tells us a טמא may eat a בכור בעל מום. A טמא is weaker than a זר when it comes to eating קדשים קלים, since a זר may eat them and a טמא may not. So if the weaker one may eat the בכור, the stronger one may too.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings of lesser holiness, like a שלמים, which a זר may eat
A non-כהן
Is it not logical? (the wording of a קל וחומר)
And if... (opening of a קל וחומר)

steps.whyThisMatters: This קל וחומר is the main logical support for בית הלל's ruling that a זר may eat a בכור בעל מום.

phrases.english: And if an impure [priest],
who may not eat offerings of lesser sanctity,
may eat from a [blemished] firstborn,
then a non-priest, who may eat offerings of lesser sanctity,
is it not logical that he may eat from a firstborn?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה טָמֵא שֶׁאֵינוֹ אוֹכֵל בְּקָדָשִׁים קַלִּים אוֹכֵל בִּבְכוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the פסוק quoted in step 1 to extend the permission from a טמא to a זר.
steps.raayaObject: That a זר may eat a בכור בעל מום
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from a טמא כהן, who the פסוק allows to eat a בכור בעל מום

steps.title: Breaking the קל וחומר: an impure כהן is allowed in communal service
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the קל וחומר: a טמא has a special strength, because טומאה is allowed in עבודת צבור, which is never true of a זר.
steps.simpleTranslation: This can be refuted: What about an impure כהן? He is special, because his general prohibition was lifted for communal service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the קל וחומר by showing that a טמא is stronger than a זר in one way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works if the starting case is weaker in every way. Here the טמא has an advantage: when there are no pure כהנים, a טמא כהן may do the public service. A זר can never do the service, so maybe the טמא is the stronger one after all.

keyTerms.meaning: This can be refuted (breaking a קל וחומר)
Was permitted out of its general prohibition
The service of communal offerings

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge does not say a טמא may eat more than a זר. It points to an advantage in service at the מזבח, which is a different area.

phrases.english: This can be refuted:
What is notable about an impure [priest]?
That his general prohibition was permitted
for communal service!
phrases.notes: When no pure כהנים are available, a טמא כהן may serve for public offerings, but a זר never may.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the קל וחומר of step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The קל וחומר from a טמא to a זר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The starting case (טמא) has an advantage the end case (זר) lacks: it is permitted in עבודת צבור. So the טמא is not clearly weaker.

steps.title: בית הלל: the topic is eating, and a non-כהן is stronger in eating
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל answer that the קל וחומר is about eating, not service, and in eating a זר is stronger than a טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל would answer: Are we talking about service? We are talking about eating, and in eating a non-כהן is stronger.
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל defend their קל וחומר by saying the challenge comes from the wrong area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is who may eat a בכור, so we only compare eating rights. A זר may eat קדשים קלים and a טמא may not, so in eating the זר is clearly stronger. The advantage of the טמא in service does not matter here, and the קל וחומר stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say...? (rejecting an assumption)
Service at the מזבח
Eating
Is superior / stronger

steps.whatToRemember: בית הלל allow a זר to eat a בכור בעל מום, based on a קל וחומר from a טמא. The קל וחומר holds because we only compare eating, where a זר is stronger.

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel [would respond]:
Is that to say it was stated about service?
We are speaking about eating,
and the eating of a non-priest is superior.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3 and saves the קל וחומר of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the comparison to the relevant area (eating, not service)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The טמא's advantage in עבודת צבור shows he is stronger than a זר, so the קל וחומר fails.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only eating rights matter here. In eating, a זר is stronger than a טמא, so the קל וחומר works.

steps.title: Why does רבי עקיבא allow even a gentile?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's report that according to רבי עקיבא even a גוי may eat a בכור בעל מום, and asks for his source.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא permits it, even to a gentile. What is the reason of רבי עקיבא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new line of the ברייתא and asks why רבי עקיבא goes so far as to allow a גוי. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Allowing a זר is one thing, but a גוי is much further away from קדושה. The גמרא wants a source for this bigger step.

keyTerms.meaning: Permits
A non-Jew
What is the reason?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva permits [it],
and even [to] a gentile.
What is the reason of Rabbi Akiva?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from בית הלל's reasoning to the next line of the ברייתא about רבי עקיבא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for רבי עקיבא's view that even a גוי may eat a בכור בעל מום.

steps.title: Like a gazelle and a deer: permitted to a gentile
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא learns from 'כצבי וכאיל': just as a deer and gazelle may be eaten by a גוי, so may blemished קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'Like the gazelle and like the deer.' Just as a gazelle and a deer are permitted to a gentile, so too disqualified offerings are permitted to a gentile.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק that compares a blemished בכור to a gazelle and a deer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says a blemished animal of קדשים is eaten 'like the gazelle and the deer', which is ordinary non-holy meat. Anyone, even a גוי, may eat a gazelle or deer. So רבי עקיבא says the same is true for these blemished animals.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the gazelle and like the deer
Disqualified (blemished) offerings
Just as... so too (a comparison)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא allows even a גוי to eat a בכור בעל מום, because the תורה compares it to a gazelle and a deer, which anyone may eat.

phrases.english: "Like the gazelle and like the deer":
just as a gazelle and a deer are permitted to a gentile,
so too disqualified [offerings] are permitted to a gentile.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״כַּצְּבִי וְכָאַיָּל״ — מָה צְבִי וְאַיָּל מוּתָּר לְגוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'כצבי וכאיל' compares blemished offerings to a gazelle and deer, which a גוי may eat. So a גוי may eat them too.

steps.title: What does the other תנא do with 'צבי ואיל'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about the תנא who disagrees with רבי עקיבא: how does he use the words 'צבי ואיל'?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the תנא who does not let a גוי eat a blemished בכור and asks what he learns from 'כצבי וכאיל'. This one word sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא used 'כצבי וכאיל' to teach that even a גוי may eat a blemished בכור. If the other תנא does not learn this, the גמרא wants to know what he does with those words. A פסוק is not supposed to sit unused.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (the other opinion)
Gazelle and deer, the wild animals the תורה compares blemished קדשים to

phrases.english: And the other one?
phrases.notes: He means the תנא who argues with רבי עקיבא and does not allow a גוי to eat it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the opposing view handles the פסוק that רבי עקיבא just used
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the other תנא learns from 'צבי ואיל' if not that a גוי may eat it

steps.title: 'צבי ואיל' is written three times, each for another lesson
steps.stepSummary: The words 'צבי ואיל' appear three times. One teaches the lesson of רבי יצחק, one the lesson of רבי אושעיא, and one the lesson of רבי אלעזר הקפר.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Deer and gazelle' is written three times. One is for the teaching of רבי יצחק, one is for the teaching of רבי אושעיא, and one is for the teaching of רבי אלעזר הקפר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the other תנא needs all the times 'צבי ואיל' appears for other lessons. So no extra mention is left over to teach about a גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other תנא is not ignoring the פסוק. He says each mention of 'צבי ואיל' is already taken by a different teaching. With nothing left over, he has no source to permit a גוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Three
They are written (in the תורה)
For the teaching of רבי so-and-so

phrases.english: 'Deer and gazelle' is written three times,
one is for the teaching of Rabbi Yitzchak,
and one is for the teaching of Rabbi Oshaya,
and one is for the teaching of Rabbi Elazar HaKappar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Every mention of 'צבי ואיל' is already used for another teaching, so none is left to permit a גוי

steps.title: One more lesson: disqualified קדשים are exempt from בכורה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another lesson from 'צבי ואיל': just as wild animals are exempt from בכורה, so are פסולי המוקדשין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one? Just as a gazelle and a deer are exempt from the law of the firstborn, so too disqualified consecrated animals are exempt from the law of the firstborn.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more teaching that comes from the comparison to 'צבי ואיל'. It shows that this comparison is used for a law about בכורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wild animals like a deer are not included in the law of בכור. Since the תורה compares פסולי המוקדשין to them, their firstborn offspring are also exempt. This is one more lesson drawn from the comparison, so it cannot also be used to permit a גוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempt
The law that a firstborn animal is holy and given to the כהן
Consecrated animals that became disqualified (for example, through a blemish) and were redeemed

phrases.english: And the other one?
phrases.notes: Here this word brings one more lesson that is learned from 'צבי ואיל'.

phrases.aramaic: מָה צְבִי וְאַיָּל פְּטוּרִים מִן הַבְּכוֹרָה,
phrases.english: just as a gazelle and a deer are exempt from the firstborn law,

phrases.aramaic: אַף פְּסוּלֵי הַמּוּקְדָּשִׁין פְּטוּרִין מִן הַבְּכוֹרָה.
phrases.english: so too disqualified consecrated animals are exempt from the firstborn law.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה צְבִי וְאַיָּל פְּטוּרִים מִן הַבְּכוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another teaching drawn from 'צבי ואיל'
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The comparison also teaches that פסולי המוקדשין are exempt from בכורה
steps.whatToRemember: Each mention of 'צבי ואיל' carries its own lesson. רבי עקיבא learns from it that a גוי may eat a blemished בכור, while the other תנא uses those mentions for other laws.

steps.title: A ברייתא: may a בכור be fed to נדות?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings a מחלוקת: בית שמאי say a blemished בכור may not be fed to נדות, and בית הלל say it may.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: A firstborn may not be fed to women who are נדות. These are the words of בית שמאי. And בית הלל say: It may be fed to נדות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ברייתא about whether impure women may eat a blemished בכור. בית שמאי forbid it and בית הלל permit it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the theme of who may eat a blemished בכור, now focusing on people who are impure. בית שמאי still treat it like holy food that must be eaten in purity. בית הלל treat it like ordinary meat in this respect.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught (introduces a ברייתא)
We feed / give to eat
Women who are impure because of menstruation

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
a firstborn may not be fed to women who are נדות,
phrases.notes: The case is a בכור that has a blemish, as the end of the discussion makes clear.

phrases.english: these are the words of Beit Shammai.
And Beit Hillel say:
it may be fed to נדות.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן בְּכוֹר אֵין מַאֲכִילִין אוֹתוֹ לְנִדּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new ברייתא on a related question about eating a blemished בכור
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי forbid feeding a blemished בכור to נדות, and בית הלל permit it

steps.title: What is בית שמאי's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of בית שמאי, who forbid feeding the בכור to נדות.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of בית שמאי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where בית שמאי get their rule from. This sets up the פסוק in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemished בכור may be eaten outside the מקדש, so it looks like ordinary meat. The גמרא wants to know why בית שמאי still keep impure people away from it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason of Beit Shammai?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of בית שמאי's ruling in the ברייתא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural basis for forbidding a בכור to נדות

steps.title: בית שמאי learn from 'ובשרם יהיה לך'
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק compares the meat of the בכור to the חזה ושוק. Just as נדות may not eat those, they may not eat the בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And their flesh shall be yours.' Just as there, נדות may not eat, so too here, נדות may not eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives בית שמאי's source: a פסוק that compares the בכור to the חזה ושוק. Since impure people may not eat the חזה ושוק, they may not eat the בכור either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about the בכור links its meat to the חזה ושוק of a שלמים. Those portions are holy and may not be eaten by someone who is impure. בית שמאי apply the same rule to the בכור, even a blemished one.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And their flesh shall be yours', a פסוק about the בכור
There (the other case)
Here (our case)

phrases.english: as it is written: 'And their flesh shall be yours,'
phrases.notes: במדבר 18:18. The פסוק goes on: 'like the breast of the waving and the right thigh.'

phrases.english: just as there, נדות may not eat,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the חזה ושוק, the parts the פסוק compares the בכור to.

phrases.english: so too here, נדות may not eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The comparison of the בכור to the חזה ושוק means impure people may not eat it

steps.title: בית הלל: that comparison is only about a בכור תם
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל answer that the comparison to חזה ושוק applies only to an unblemished בכור. For a בעל מום, the תורה says 'הטמא והטהור יאכלנו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל? This applies only to an unblemished one. But a blemished one: 'The impure and the pure may eat it.'
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל explain why they do not accept בית שמאי's proof. The comparison is about a בכור without a blemish, and the תורה clearly allows anyone to eat a blemished one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל agree with the פסוק but limit its scope to a בכור תם. For a בכור בעל מום there is a separate פסוק that lets impure and pure people eat it alike. So נדות may eat it.

keyTerms.meaning: This applies only to... (limits a rule)
An unblemished animal
An animal with a blemish
'The impure and the pure may eat it'

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel [would respond]:
This applies only to an unblemished one,
but a blemished one —
'the impure and the pure may eat it.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: בית הלל limit the scope of בית שמאי's פסוק
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a פסוק to a narrower case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'ובשרם יהיה לך' covers every בכור, so no impure person may eat any בכור
steps.terutzMaskana: The comparison to חזה ושוק covers only a בכור תם; a blemished בכור may be eaten by the impure and the pure
steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי treat a blemished בכור like holy meat that must be eaten in purity. בית הלל say a blemished בכור may be eaten even by impure people, because of 'הטמא והטהור יאכלנו'.
steps.confusionAlert: בית הלל do not reject the comparison to חזה ושוק. They only say it applies to a בכור תם, not to a בעל מום.

steps.title: בית שמאי limit the verse to outside impurity
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי answer that 'הטמא והטהור יאכלנו' only allows people whose טומאה came from outside, not those whose טומאה comes from their own body.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית שמאי would say: that פסוק only applies where the טומאה does not come out of the person's own body. But where the טומאה comes out of his own body, it does not apply.
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל just quoted 'הטמא והטהור יאכלנו' to allow even נדות to eat a blemished בכור. Now the גמרא explains how בית שמאי deal with that same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי agree that some טמאים may eat a blemished בכור. But they read 'טמא' as only someone who caught טומאה from outside, like a טמא מת. A נדה or a זב, whose טומאה comes from inside the body, is not included, so they still may not eat it.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply (only in this case)
Impurity that comes out of the person's own body (like a זב or a נדה)
Where, in a case where

steps.confusionAlert: בית שמאי are not rejecting the פסוק 'הטמא והטהור יאכלנו'. They accept it but narrow who it covers.

phrases.english: And בית שמאי would say: these words apply

phrases.aramaic: הֵיכָא דְּאֵין טוּמְאָה יוֹצְאָה עָלָיו מִגּוּפוֹ,
phrases.english: where the impurity does not come out on him from his own body,
but where the impurity
comes out on him from his own body, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers בית הלל's פסוק from step 13 by narrowing its scope.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'הטמא' seems to include every kind of טמא, even a נדה.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'הטמא' includes only people whose טומאה came from outside, so נדות still may not eat.

steps.title: Proof from קרבן פסח that the תורה splits the two kinds of impurity
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי show that the תורה does tell apart inner and outer טומאה: a פסח brought in טומאה may not be eaten by זבים, מצורעים, נדות and יולדות.
steps.simpleTranslation: For we find that the תורה makes a difference between טומאה that comes from one's own body and טומאה that does not. As the משנה teaches: when the פסח is brought in a state of טומאה, זבים, מצורעים, זבות, נדות and יולדות may not eat from it.
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי back up their split by showing that the תורה already uses it somewhere else, by קרבן פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When most of the people are טמא מת, the פסח may be brought and eaten in טומאה. Yet the משנה still forbids people whose טומאה comes from their own bodies. So the תורה does treat the two types differently, and בית שמאי apply the same split to בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: We find
The Torah (literally 'the Merciful One') distinguishes
A קרבן פסח offered while the people are טמא
People with a bodily discharge, and people with צרעת
Women who have just given birth

phrases.english: For we find that the Merciful One distinguishes
between impurity that comes out on him from his own body,

phrases.aramaic: לְבֵין שֶׁאֵין טוּמְאָה יוֹצְאָה עָלָיו מִגּוּפוֹ,
phrases.english: and impurity that does not come out on him from his own body,
as we learned in a משנה: the פסח that is brought in impurity,
זבים and מצורעים may not eat from it,
nor זבות, נדות, or women after childbirth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports בית שמאי's split from step 14.
steps.raayaObject: The Torah treats inner (bodily) טומאה differently from outer טומאה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה (פסחים 95b): a פסח brought in טומאה may not be eaten by זבים, מצורעים, זבות, נדות and יולדות.

steps.title: בית הלל: the פסח split comes from a special word
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל reject the proof. By פסח the תורה wrote 'טמא נפש', but by בכור it just says 'טמא', so every kind of טמא is included.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל would say: there, by פסח, the תורה spelled out 'טמא נפש'. But here it just writes 'טמא' with no detail, so there is no difference.
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל push back on בית שמאי's proof from פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By פסח, the תורה itself named one kind of טומאה, 'טמא נפש', so only that kind is allowed. By בכור, the פסוק says 'טמא' with no detail. So there is no reason to copy the פסח split over, and a נדה may eat a blemished בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah revealed, spelled out
Impure from a dead body
Plainly, without details
There is no difference

steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי: only outer טומאה may eat a blemished בכור, learned from פסח. בית הלל: the plain word 'טמא' by בכור includes all טמאים, and the פסח split comes only from the special words 'טמא נפש'.

phrases.english: And בית הלל would say: it is only there
that the Merciful One spelled out 'impure from a dead body',
but here 'impure' is written plainly,
there is no difference.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית הִלֵּל: הָתָם הוּא דְּגַלִּי רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from פסח brought in step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison from פסח to בכור
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסח split comes from the special wording 'טמא נפש', which the בכור פסוק does not have.

steps.title: No skinning from the feet on יום טוב, or for a בכור or פסולי המוקדשין
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: one may not skin an animal from its feet on יום טוב, and the same is true for a בכור and for פסולי המוקדשין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: one may not skin from the feet on יום טוב. In the same way, one may not skin a בכור from the feet, nor פסולי המוקדשין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ברייתא about a way of skinning an animal called מרגילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מרגילין means skinning the animal starting from the feet, so the hide comes off whole. The ברייתא forbids this on יום טוב, and it puts a בכור and פסולי המוקדשין in the same group, even though they are not about יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Skinning an animal starting from its feet, keeping the hide whole
A festival day
Similarly, in the same way
The רבנן taught (introduces a ברייתא)

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין מַרְגִּילִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: The Sages taught: one may not skin from the feet on a Festival,
phrases.notes: Peeling the skin off starting from the feet, so the hide stays whole like a bag.

phrases.english: similarly, one may not skin a firstborn from the feet,
nor disqualified consecrated animals.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין מַרְגִּילִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the נדות discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Skinning from the feet (מרגילין) is forbidden on יום טוב, and also for a בכור and for פסולי המוקדשין.

steps.title: The יום טוב case makes sense, but who taught the בכור case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that skinning from the feet is forbidden on יום טוב, because it is extra work not needed for the day. It then asks which תנא holds that this is also forbidden for a בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense on יום טוב, since he is doing extra work that the day does not need. But for a בכור, which תנא taught this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts working through the ברייתא from step 17. It agrees with the first case and asks who the author of the second case is. This question sets up רב חסדא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום טוב you may only do work that is needed for the day. Skinning from the feet is extra effort, done only to keep the hide whole, so it is clearly forbidden. A blemished בכור has no יום טוב problem, so the גמרא needs to know why skinning it this way would be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / Granted (the first case is understood)
Effort that is not fit or needed for that day
Which תנא taught this? (Who is the author?)

phrases.english: Granted, on a Festival:

phrases.aramaic: דְּקָא טָרַח טִירְחָא דְּלָא חֲזֵי לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: because he is putting in effort that is not needed for it.
But a firstborn: who is the תנא who taught this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the ברייתא quoted in step 17, clause by clause.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא forbids skinning a בכור from its feet?

steps.title: רב חסדא: the בכור case follows בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that the בכור clause follows בית שמאי. They said a blemished בכור may not be fed to נדות, which shows they treat it as holy meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: It is בית שמאי, who say that we may not feed it to נדות.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא identifies the author of the בכור clause as בית שמאי, linking it back to their argument earlier on the daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier (steps 10–16), בית שמאי held that a blemished בכור may not be eaten by people whose טומאה comes from their own body, such as נדות. This shows that for them it still keeps a holy status like a קרבן. So it should not be handled like ordinary meat, and skinning it from the feet is not proper.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of שמאי
We may not feed (it to someone)
Women who are טמא from menstruation

steps.whyThisMatters: It ties this ברייתא back to the מחלוקת between בית שמאי and בית הלל, so the ruling does not follow the accepted view of בית הלל.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said:
It is Beit Shammai,
who say that one may not feed it to menstruating women.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The author is בית שמאי, who give a blemished בכור the status of holy meat.

steps.title: Who taught the case of פסולי המוקדשין?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next clause of the ברייתא, that skinning from the feet is also forbidden for פסולי המוקדשין, and asks who its author is.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And not with פסולי המוקדשין." Which תנא taught this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the third case in the ברייתא and asks the same question again. This sets up רב חסדא's second answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פסולי המוקדשין are sacrifices that got a מום and were redeemed, so they are normally eaten like ordinary meat. The גמרא wants to know who still treats them as holy enough to forbid skinning them from the feet.

keyTerms.meaning: Sacrificial animals that became unfit (usually through a מום) and were redeemed

phrases.english: "And not with disqualified consecrated animals."
Who is the תנא who taught this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same kind of question as step 18, now about the third clause.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא forbids skinning פסולי המוקדשין from the feet?

steps.title: רב חסדא: it follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says this clause follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, and introduces a source to show his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: It is רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, as we learned:
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא names the author and says "as we learned," which introduces the source in the next steps that shows this תנא's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name by itself does not prove anything yet. The proof comes from a teaching about two חטאות, where רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון shows that a blemished sacrifice keeps holiness even after it is slaughtered.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא, son of רבי שמעון בר יוחאי
As we learned (introduces a quoted source)

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said:
It is Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon,
as we learned:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא, דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The author is רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.

steps.title: The case of two חטאות: one תמימה, one with a מום
steps.stepSummary: The quoted source describes a person with two חטאות, one unblemished and one blemished. The unblemished one is brought and the blemished one is redeemed. If the blemished one is slaughtered before the blood of the unblemished one is thrown, it is permitted. If it is slaughtered after, it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone had two חטאות, one unblemished and one with a מום, the unblemished one is offered and the blemished one is redeemed. If the blemished one was slaughtered before the blood of the unblemished one was thrown, it is permitted. If it was slaughtered after the blood was thrown, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first part of the source רב חסדא quoted. It gives the basic ruling of the first opinion, and the next step adds רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the owner gets כפרה through the blood of the unblemished חטאת, the leftover one becomes a חטאת that has to be left to die, and it is forbidden. According to this first opinion, what matters is the time of slaughter. If the blemished animal was already slaughtered before the כפרה, it is ordinary permitted meat.

keyTerms.meaning: Sin offerings
Unblemished (fit for the מזבח)
Blemished
Should be redeemed
Its blood was thrown on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: Both animals are חטאות of the same person. The point is that once he gets כפרה from one, the other one becomes forbidden.

phrases.english: If he had before him two sin offerings,
one unblemished and one blemished,
the unblemished one is sacrificed, and the blemished one is redeemed.
If the blemished one was slaughtered,

phrases.aramaic: אִם עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִזְרַק דָּמָהּ שֶׁל תְּמִימָה — מוּתֶּרֶת,
phrases.english: if this was before the blood of the unblemished one was thrown, it is permitted;

phrases.aramaic: אִם מִשֶּׁנִּזְרַק דָּמָהּ שֶׁל תְּמִימָה — אֲסוּרָה.
phrases.english: if it was after the blood of the unblemished one was thrown, it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source introduced by דִּתְנַן in step 21.
steps.raayaObject: Background ruling needed to understand רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's view.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching about two חטאות, one of them blemished.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון: even meat already in the pot becomes forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says that even if the blemished animal's meat is already cooking in the pot when the blood of the unblemished one is thrown, it becomes forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says: Even if the meat is in the pot, and then the blood of the unblemished one is thrown, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the line that proves רב חסדא's point. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds that a blemished sacrifice keeps its holy status even after it is slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the first opinion, slaughter turns a redeemed blemished animal into ordinary meat. For רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, the meat still counts as a חטאת until it is eaten, so it can still become forbidden later. Since he treats פסולי המוקדשין as holy even after slaughter, he would also forbid skinning them from the feet, just like the ברייתא says.

keyTerms.meaning: Meat already in the pot (slaughtered and cooking)
Forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא about skinning from the feet follows minority views: בית שמאי for a בכור, and רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון for פסולי המוקדשין. Both treat a blemished holy animal as still holy.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the ban on skinning from the feet depends on how much holiness a blemished sacrifice keeps.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, says:
Even if the meat is in the pot,
and then the blood of the unblemished one was thrown, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ בָּשָׂר בִּקְדֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion of step 22 and completes רב חסדא's proof.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's claim that the פסולי המוקדשין clause follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.raayaSupportSource: His ruling that even slaughtered, cooking meat of a blemished חטאת becomes forbidden, which shows it keeps its holiness after slaughter.

steps.title: Why not attribute the whole ברייתא to בית שמאי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא: why split the ברייתא between two authors? Let him say all of it follows בית שמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא should explain the entire ברייתא according to בית שמאי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רב חסדא's approach. He said the ברייתא has two different authors, and the גמרא asks why he didn't just say one author, בית שמאי, for all of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רב חסדא said the בכור clause follows בית שמאי and the פסולי המוקדשין clause follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. Splitting one ברייתא between two authors is awkward. If בית שמאי treat a blemished בכור as holy meat, maybe they treat פסולי המוקדשין the same way, and then one author would cover everything.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him establish it, meaning let him explain the source as following a certain view
All of it, the entire ברייתא
The school of שמאי, often stricter than בית הלל

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב חִסְדָּא, לוֹקְמַהּ כּוּלַּהּ כְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי!
phrases.english: But רב חסדא should establish all of it according to בית שמאי!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב חִסְדָּא, לוֹקְמַהּ כּוּלַּהּ כְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the two-author attribution that רב חסדא set up in steps 19 and 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's assigning the second clause to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון instead of to בית שמאי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It is simpler to have one author for a whole ברייתא. If בית שמאי already hold the strict view for a בכור, they could be the author of the פסולי המוקדשין clause too.

steps.title: בית שמאי may be strict only with a בכור
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that בית שמאי's view may be limited to a בכור, whose holiness begins at birth. פסולי המוקדשין only became holy later, so בית שמאי may not be strict about them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps בית שמאי said their ruling only about a בכור, because its holiness is from the womb. But פסולי המוקדשין, whose holiness is not from the womb, perhaps they do not include.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב חסדא. It explains that we cannot be sure בית שמאי would say the same thing about פסולי המוקדשין, so רב חסדא needed a different author for that clause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור is holy from the moment it is born, so its holiness is especially strong. That may be why בית שמאי still treat it as holy meat even after it gets a blemish. A regular animal that was dedicated and then became blemished only became holy when a person dedicated it, so בית שמאי's reasoning might not apply to it. That is why רב חסדא used רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who clearly holds a strict view in a case of פסולי המוקדשין.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps, maybe
They only said their ruling up to this point, meaning their view is limited to this case
Its holiness is from the womb, holy from birth
Dedicated animals that became disqualified, usually through a blemish

steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא needs two authors because a בכור's holiness starts at birth, which makes it stronger. בית שמאי's strict view about a בכור may not carry over to פסולי המוקדשין.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up an important difference: holiness that comes from birth may be stronger than holiness that comes from a person dedicating the animal.

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי
phrases.english: Perhaps בית שמאי only said their ruling
about a בכור,
because its holiness is from the womb,
but disqualified dedicated animals,
whose holiness is not from the womb, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אֶלָּא בִּבְכוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 24 by limiting בית שמאי's view to a בכור.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting a view to its case: בית שמאי's ruling may apply only to a בכור
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בית שמאי's strict view about a blemished בכור might apply to all פסולי המוקדשין, so one author could cover the whole ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: A בכור's holiness from birth may be uniquely strong. We cannot assume בית שמאי hold the same about פסולי המוקדשין, so רב חסדא needed רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון for that clause.
